human_summary: This material provides a comprehensive overview of the BI-RADS Mammography Lexicon and detailed information on breast density. It covers the classification of mammographic findings, the definition and categories of breast density, relevant FDA legislation, assessment methodologies, and the clinical significance of density regarding mammographic accuracy and breast cancer risk. The text is medium in volume, rich in classifications, facts, and concepts, and includes numerous illustrative images of breast density categories.

educational_units.title: Term: BI-RADS Mammography Lexicon
educational_units.description: The structured reporting system for mammography findings, providing standardized terminology.

educational_units.title: Classification: Breast Tissue Density Categories (A, B, C, D)
educational_units.description: Four categories describing breast composition from almost entirely fatty (A) to extremely dense (D), with implications for mammography sensitivity.

factual_anchors.value: Classification: Breast Tissue Density Categories (A, B, C, D)

educational_units.title: Classification: Mass Characteristics
educational_units.description: Sub-categories for mass shape (oval, lobulated, round, irregular), margin (circumscribed, obscured, indistinct, spiculated), and density (fat-containing, low, equal, high).

educational_units.title: Classification: Calcification Types & Distribution
educational_units.description: Categories for typically benign, suspicious morphology (amorphous, pleomorphic, linear), and distribution (diffuse, regional, grouped, linear, segmental).

educational_units.title: Classification: Other Mammographic Findings
educational_units.description: Categories for architectural distortion, asymmetries, lymph nodes, skin lesions, dilated ducts, associated features, special cases, and location of findings.

educational_units.title: Concept: Definition of Breast Density
educational_units.description: The relative proportion of breast parenchyma to fat, where parenchyma is radiodense and fat is radiolucent on mammography.
educational_units.evidence: Breast density is defined as the relative proportion of breast parenchyma to fat...

educational_units.title: Fact: FDA Legislation on Breast Density Reporting
educational_units.description: Reporting breast density is required by FDA legislation as of September 2024, with singular phrasing for unilateral mammograms approved in July 2025.
educational_units.evidence: Reporting breast density is required by Food and Drug Administration (FDA) legislation as of September 2024.

factual_anchors.value: Fact: FDA Legislation on Breast Density Reporting

educational_units.title: Classification: Dense vs. Non-Dense Breasts
educational_units.description: Categories C (heterogeneously dense) and D (extremely dense) are considered dense; A (almost entirely fatty) and B (scattered fibroglandular density) are non-dense.
educational_units.evidence: People with heterogeneously dense or extremely dense breasts are considered to have dense breasts...

educational_units.title: Process: Breast Density Assessment Methods
educational_units.description: Breast density is commonly assessed by subjective visual inspection, though FDA-approved automated density measurement software is available.
educational_units.evidence: Most commonly, the interpreting radiologist subjectively categorizes... although FDA-approved automated density measurement software is available.

educational_units.title: Fact: BI-RADS 5th Edition Classification Change
educational_units.description: The classification changed from evaluating the percentage of dense tissue to assessing the likelihood that overlying tissue may obscure a cancer.
educational_units.evidence: With the BI-RADS 5th Edition, the classification of breast density changed from an evaluation of the percentage... to an assessment based on the likelihood that overlying tissue may obscure a cancer.

educational_units.title: Process: Rules for Assigning Breast Density Category
educational_units.description: The classification should be based on the region potentially masking cancer, the greater density is assigned if breasts differ, and density is updated at each examination.
educational_units.evidence: If tissue in one region is dense... then the breast density classification should be based on an assessment of this region...

factual_anchors.value: Process: Rules for Assigning Breast Density Category

educational_units.title: Concept: Variability of Breast Density
educational_units.description: Breast density can change from year to year due to factors like weight changes, estrogen replacement therapy, and menopause.
educational_units.evidence: Breast density can be variable from year to year, depending on multiple factors such as weight gain or loss, estrogen replacement therapy, menopause, etc.

educational_units.title: Concept: Significance of Breast Density (Overview)
educational_units.description: Breast density is significant due to its impact on mammographic accuracy (masking effect) and its association with an increased inherent breast cancer risk.
educational_units.evidence: Breast density is significant for two reasons: mammographic accuracy and breast cancer risk.

educational_units.title: Process: Impact on Mammographic Accuracy - Masking Effect
educational_units.description: Dense fibroglandular tissue can obscure small masses, reducing the sensitivity of mammography, especially with older technologies.
educational_units.evidence: The impact of breast density on mammographic accuracy is due to the masking effect of dense fibroglandular tissue.

factual_anchors.value: Process: Impact on Mammographic Accuracy - Masking Effect

educational_units.title: Fact: Technological Advances & Sensitivity Improvement
educational_units.description: Digital mammography and Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) have significantly reduced the masking effect and increased cancer detection rates in dense breasts.
educational_units.evidence: The masking effect... has been reduced by advances in technology, first with the adoption of digital mammography, and, more recently, with DBT.

educational_units.title: Fact: Breast Cancer Risk by Density Category (Odds Ratios)
educational_units.description: Dense breasts confer an increased inherent risk for breast cancer, with specific odds ratios provided for different density categories.
educational_units.evidence: Compared to the breasts of women with scattered fibroglandular tissue, the odds ratio of breast cancer is 0.6 for almost entirely fatty. 1.4 for heterogeneously dense, and 1.6 for extremely dense breasts.

factual_anchors.value: Fact: Breast Cancer Risk by Density Category (Odds Ratios)

educational_units.title: Visual: Identification of Breast Density Categories (A, B, C, D) from Images
educational_units.description: Recognizing the visual characteristics of each breast density category (A, B, C, D) as depicted in mammographic images.

factual_anchors.value: Visual: Identification of Breast Density Categories (A, B, C, D) from Images
